primitives.note: Lightslinger: casting any ability (Q/W/E/R) arms Lucian's next basic attack; that attack fires an additional shot 0.25s later for bonus physical damage (or bonus magic damage if a separate Vigilance stack is consumed, which requires an ally heal/shield or enemy immobilize and so cannot trigger in the allyless/CC-ignored dummy fight).
Relentless Pursuit resets Lucian's basic attack timer, letting him fit an extra auto (and thus an extra Lightslinger arm/consume cycle) into the rotation.
E's current cooldown is reduced by 1s per Lightslinger shot landed on a non-champion, 2s per shot landed on the dummy (which counts as an enemy champion).
Piercing Light (0.35s bin cast time / 0.4-0.25s wiki per-rank) and Ardent Blaze (0.25s cast) each deal a single fixed damage instance on a short delay, on cooldown.
The Culling channels for up to 3s firing up to 22 bullets; Lucian cannot basic-attack while channeling (attack=false during channel per the interaction table).

The Culling can be recast after 0.75s to end the channel early, and auto-recasts to end itself when the 3s duration completes; each of the up-to-22 bullets is its own damage instance calculated on impact.
The Culling's total bullet count scales with the caster's crit chance (bin formula also involves crit damage); this changes total R damage rather than individual hits critting.
Mana costs on Q (48-80), W (60), E (32-0), and R (100) can cap how many casts fit into a 15s window, particularly at low levels/low mana itemization.

needsBespoke.why: Every damage-relevant mechanic (the ability-cast-arms-next-auto passive, E's attack reset and cooldown refund, Q/W flat-damage casts, R's channel/recast/crit-scaled shot count, and mana gating) maps onto an existing primitive. Vigilance (the heal/shield/immobilize-triggered magic-damage empowered shots) is part of the same passive but its triggers (ally heal/shield, enemy immobilize/CC) either require an ally or are CC, both absent/ignored in the specified 1v1 dummy and survival fights, so it can be omitted from the modeled damage rather than requiring new mechanics.

proposal: Open with a basic attack to establish the auto-attack rhythm.

Weave an ability cast (Q, then W, then E as each becomes available) immediately after each basic attack so the ability's cast arms Lightslinger and the very next auto fires the bonus-damage second shot.

Use Relentless Pursuit (E) right after an auto attack when it is off cooldown, purely for its attack-timer reset, to squeeze in an extra auto (and Lightslinger arm/consume cycle) without losing tempo; its own cooldown is further cut by Lightslinger hits landing on the dummy.
Fire Piercing Light (Q) and Ardent Blaze (W) on cooldown, sequencing them so their cast times don't stack idle time on top of the auto-attack weave.

Cast The Culling (R) as soon as it is available and channel it to completion (or until mana runs out) for its high sustained multi-hit damage, since only one R cast fits in the 15s window on its long cooldown.
For the remainder of the fight, continue the auto+Q/W/E weave, prioritizing whichever of Q/W/E is off cooldown and always following a cast with an auto to consume the Lightslinger arm.
If mana is exhausted, fall back to auto attacks only until a cost-bearing ability's cooldown and mana allow resuming the weave.
questions: Should R be cast at the very start of the fight to guarantee it lands, or held slightly to line up with a Lightslinger-armed auto/crit itemization for maximum total shot count, given only one R cast fits in a 15s window?

Can the simulator model perfect ability-into-auto weaving (zero cancel/animation overhead between an ability's cast finishing and the next auto firing), or is there a tempo cost that should reduce how many Lightslinger procs fit into 15s?
At what level/item state should mana be assumed sufficient to sustain the full Q/W/E/R weave for the entire 15s, versus needing to skip casts due to mana starvation?
